skill.name: github-issue-creator
skill.description: Turn error logs, screenshots, voice notes, and rough bug reports into crisp, developer-ready GitHub issues with repro steps, impact, and evidence.
skill.summary: Convert messy bug input into structured GitHub issue drafts with reproduction steps, impact, and evidence.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Teams often receive vague bug notes, error logs, and screenshots that are hard to triage. This skill turns that input into structured GitHub issue drafts with evidence and impact.
actual_capabilities: Transforms rough bug notes into structured GitHub issue drafts.
Extracts summary, environment, reproduction steps, expected behavior, and actual behavior.
Classifies impact as critical, high, medium, or low based on user-provided context.
References screenshots and GIFs as inline evidence in the issue body.
Uses placeholders for sensitive values such as project names and user identifiers.
Saves issue drafts as Markdown files under the repository issues directory.
limitations: It does not verify whether the bug can be reproduced.
It cannot create GitHub issues through the GitHub API by itself.
It depends on the quality and completeness of the provided input.
It may need clarification when environment details or success criteria are missing.

use_cases.title: Triage Support Reports
use_cases.description: Convert customer support notes into issue drafts that engineers can review quickly.

use_cases.title: Document QA Failures
use_cases.description: Turn test failures, screenshots, and reproduction notes into consistent issue reports.

use_cases.title: Capture Developer Bugs
use_cases.description: Create clear issue drafts from error logs, terminal output, and incomplete bug notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue from this bug note. Include a clear summary, reproduction steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, and impact: [paste note]

prompt_templates.title: Use Error Logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this error log into a GitHub issue draft. Preserve important error details and replace sensitive values with placeholders: [paste log]

prompt_templates.title: Combine Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an issue from these notes and screenshot descriptions. Reference each attachment inline and explain the user impact: [paste notes and attachment names]

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Triage Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these related bug reports and create separate GitHub issue drafts. Group duplicate evidence, assign severity, and ask for missing details when needed: [paste reports]

output_examples.input: A voice note says deployment finished, but the agent disappeared from the list and no error appeared.
output_examples.output: A GitHub issue draft with a silent deployment failure summary, reproduction steps, expected listing behavior, actual disappearance, and high impact.

output_examples.input: An error paste shows PERMISSION_DENIED code 403 when publishing to a Teams channel.
output_examples.output: A structured issue draft describing the 403 publishing failure, missing environment details, expected successful publish, and blocked integration impact.

output_examples.input: A tester provides screenshots showing a broken dashboard chart after applying a date filter.
output_examples.output: An issue draft that references the screenshots, lists filter steps, explains the incorrect chart behavior, and requests version details.

best_practices: Provide the original error text, screenshots, and affected environment details.
Review generated issue drafts before filing them in a shared tracker.
Replace or confirm sensitive values before sharing the issue outside the team.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for tasks that are not bug or issue documentation.
Do not publish generated issues without checking facts and reproduction steps.
Do not include secrets, customer identifiers, or private project names in issue drafts.

faq.question: Does this skill create issues directly in GitHub?
faq.answer: No. It creates Markdown issue drafts that can be reviewed and copied into GitHub.

faq.question: Can it process screenshots or GIFs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reference provided attachments and describe them as visual evidence in the issue draft.

faq.question: Does it protect sensitive information?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to replace sensitive values with placeholders, but users should still review every draft.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Error logs, support notes, reproduction notes, screenshots, voice dictation, and environment details work best.

faq.question: Can it assign severity?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps severity to impact using critical, high, medium, and low categories.

faq.question: When should I ask for clarification?
faq.answer: Ask for clarification when reproduction steps, affected environment, permissions, or expected behavior are missing.
